# @moku-labs/system — full reference

Isomorphic system API for Moku — store, tray, notify, clipboard, and deep-link
capabilities behind an env-style provider seam (Tauri provider when the native shell is
detected, web fallback otherwise). Same island code runs on web and native. Built on
@moku-labs/core 1.5.0 (micro-kernel) and @moku-labs/common 0.3.0 (logPlugin -> ctx.log,
envPlugin -> ctx.env). Package: @moku-labs/system 0.1.0.

Contents:
  1. Entry points & exports
  2. The SystemResult contract (src/plugins/runtime/result.ts)
  3. Runtime core plugin (ctx.runtime)
  4. Capability plugins: full public types
     4.1 store  4.2 tray  4.3 notify  4.4 clipboard  4.5 deepLink
  5. Event catalog
  6. Config schema & defaults (pluginConfigs)
  7. Lifecycle & provider resolution semantics
  8. Error-handling patterns
  9. Usage examples
  10. Extension pattern (createPlugin)
  11. Peer dependencies, web bundling & environment
  12. Native permissions (Tauri ACL) & cross-repo naming

====================================================================
1. Entry points & exports
====================================================================

Root entry "@moku-labs/system" (src/index.ts) — helpers + TYPES ONLY, zero capability code:

  export const createApp     // create a system app (Layer 3 entry point)
  export const createPlugin  // define a consumer (Layer 3) plugin bound to this framework
  export { err, ok }         // SystemResult constructors (from ./plugins/runtime/result)
  export type * as Store     from "./plugins/store/types";
  export type * as Tray      from "./plugins/tray/types";
  export type * as Notify    from "./plugins/notify/types";
  export type * as Clipboard from "./plugins/clipboard/types";
  export type * as DeepLink  from "./plugins/deep-link/types";
  export type { JsonPrimitive, JsonValue, RuntimeKind, RuntimePlatform,
                SystemErr, SystemErrorReason, SystemOk, SystemResult };

Subpath entries — plugin INSTANCES live here (D-011b: the root barrel leaked ~2 KB gz of
unimported capability code — measured; import instances from subpaths so unused
capabilities never enter your bundle):

  "@moku-labs/system/store"     -> export { storePlugin };     export type * as Store;
  "@moku-labs/system/tray"      -> export { trayPlugin };      export type * as Tray;
  "@moku-labs/system/notify"    -> export { notifyPlugin };    export type * as Notify;
  "@moku-labs/system/clipboard" -> export { clipboardPlugin }; export type * as Clipboard;
  "@moku-labs/system/deep-link" -> export { deepLinkPlugin };  export type * as DeepLink;

All entries ship ESM (+ CJS) with types; "sideEffects": false.

====================================================================
2. The SystemResult contract (src/plugins/runtime/result.ts)
====================================================================

The uniform outcome contract for every capability method — never a thrown surprise
inside a webview. Programmer errors still throw normally.

  /** The active shell kind a provider was selected for. */
  export type RuntimeKind = "tauri" | "web";

  /** OS platform within the kind. "unknown" is the honest fallback (incl. SSR). */
  export type RuntimePlatform = "macos" | "windows" | "linux" | "ios" | "android" | "unknown";

  /** JSON-safe primitive. */
  export type JsonPrimitive = string | number | boolean | null;

  /**
   * Cross-provider value domain for store — JSON files and structured clone round-trip
   * Date/Map/etc. differently, so both providers accept only JSON-safe values.
   */
  export type JsonValue = JsonPrimitive | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue };

  /** Why a capability call did not succeed. */
  export type SystemErrorReason = "unsupported" | "denied" | "unavailable" | "error";

  /** Successful outcome. */
  export type SystemOk<T> = { ok: true; value: T; provider: RuntimeKind };

  /** Failed outcome — degraded, denied, absent, or errored, as typed data. */
  export type SystemErr = {
    ok: false;
    provider: RuntimeKind;
    reason: SystemErrorReason;
    message?: string;
  };

  export type SystemResult<T> = SystemOk<T> | SystemErr;

  /** Construct a success outcome. */
  export function ok<T>(value: T, provider: RuntimeKind): SystemOk<T>;

  /** Construct a failure outcome. message is raw diagnostic text, preserved. */
  export function err(provider: RuntimeKind, reason: SystemErrorReason, message?: string): SystemErr;

Internal (not exported from the package, but part of the semantics):

  - mapThrownToResult(provider, thrown, reason = "error"): folds any thrown/rejected
    value into a SystemErr, preserving the raw message. NEVER produces "denied" —
    Tauri ACL throws are ambiguous (D-004); "denied" is reserved for unambiguous
    RETURNED permission signals. Provider-resolution paths pass "unavailable";
    method paths default to "error".
  - unsupportedProvider(provider, methods): mechanically produces a provider whose
    every listed method resolves to err(provider, "unsupported"), plus a no-op
    dispose(). The single source for BOTH absence cases: unsupported-by-kind (tray on
    web) and unsupported-by-platform-within-kind (tray on Tauri iOS/Android).

Reason semantics (the error-mapping table):

  reason        | meaning                                            | typical sources
  ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------
  "unsupported" | capability permanently absent in this environment  | tray on web; tray on Tauri
                |                                                    | mobile; navigator.clipboard
                |                                                    | absent (insecure context)
  "denied"      | unambiguous permission refusal (returned signal,   | Notification permission not
                | never inferred from a throw)                       | granted; clipboard NotAllowedError
  "unavailable" | environment cannot deliver right now               | provider failed to resolve;
                |                                                    | app not started; stopped during
                |                                                    | resolution; Safari private-mode
                |                                                    | IndexedDB write-probe failure
  "error"       | provider threw during the operation                | any unexpected native/web throw;
                |                                                    | raw message preserved in .message

====================================================================
3. Runtime core plugin (ctx.runtime)
====================================================================

Auto-registered in src/config.ts as the third core plugin alongside logPlugin +
envPlugin — every plugin's ctx carries ctx.log, ctx.env, and ctx.runtime. Detection is
synchronous, import-free, and happens once per app lifetime (createState).

src/plugins/runtime/types.ts:

  /** Runtime detection overrides — both null by default (auto-detect). */
  export type RuntimeConfig = {
    /** Force the detected shell kind. Default: null (auto-detect). */
    forceKind: RuntimeKind | null;
    /** Force the detected OS platform. Default: null (auto-detect). */
    forcePlatform: RuntimePlatform | null;
  };

  /** Internal runtime state — detection result, computed once in createState. */
  export type RuntimeState = {
    /** Detected (or forced) shell kind. Never changes for the app's lifetime. */
    kind: RuntimeKind;
    /** Detected (or forced) OS platform. */
    platform: RuntimePlatform;
  };

  /** The API injected on every regular plugin's context as ctx.runtime. */
  export type RuntimeApi = {
    readonly kind: RuntimeKind;
    readonly platform: RuntimePlatform;
  };

Detection rules (src/plugins/runtime/detect.ts):
  - kind: "tauri" when globalThis.isTauri === true OR the Tauri 2 marker
    __TAURI_INTERNALS__ is present on globalThis; "web" otherwise.
  - platform: navigator UA heuristics -> "macos" | "windows" | "linux" | "ios" |
    "android"; "unknown" when undetectable (including SSR, where navigator is absent).
  - Inside the Tauri shell a Macintosh UA with navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1 is "ios" —
    that is an iPad in desktop mode, which has no tray.
  - Browser globals are touched only inside function bodies — SSR-safe to import.

Overrides: pluginConfigs: { runtime: { forceKind, forcePlatform } } is applied from
createApp too (consumer config wins the core-plugin cascade), but `runtime` is not one of
createApp's TYPED pluginConfigs keys (those come from the plugins you compose) — hoist the
object into a const instead of inlining it (see section 9).

====================================================================
4. Capability plugins — full public types
====================================================================

All five capability plugins share the same anatomy (Complex tier): index.ts defines the
plugin via createPlugin(name, { config?, createState, api, onInit?, onStart, onStop });
onStart kicks off fire-and-forget provider resolution; every API method awaits the
resolution slot and returns SystemResult. Provider interface types are STRUCTURAL and
local — @tauri-apps/* types are never re-exported (.d.mts leakage guard).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 store — plugin name "store", subpath "@moku-labs/system/store"
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Key-value persistence, the template capability. Tauri provider persists to a store file
with an awaited save() after every mutation (durable when ok); web provider persists to
IndexedDB via idb-keyval with a one-time write-probe at resolution (Safari private
browsing -> deterministic "unavailable" instead of a random runtime throw).

src/plugins/store/types.ts:

  /** Store namespace config — maps to the Tauri store filename and IndexedDB database name. */
  export type StoreConfig = {
    /** Namespace for persisted data. File-safe, validated at onInit. Default: "moku-system". */
    name: string;
  };

  /** Internal store state — the resolution slot. */
  export type StoreState = ResolutionState<StoreProvider>;

  /**
   * Key-value persistence API. Every method returns SystemResult — environmental
   * failures are typed data, never throws.
   */
  export type StoreApi = {
    /** Read a value. ok(undefined) when the key is absent. */
    get: <T extends JsonValue = JsonValue>(key: string) => Promise<SystemResult<T | undefined>>;
    /** Write a value. Durable when the promise resolves ok (Tauri: awaited save()). */
    set: <T extends JsonValue>(key: string, value: T) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
    /** Remove a key. void (not "existed") for cross-provider parity (D-003). */
    delete: (key: string) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
    /** List all keys in the namespace. */
    keys: () => Promise<SystemResult<string[]>>;
    /** Remove all keys in the namespace. */
    clear: () => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
  };

onInit: config.name must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/i — it becomes a filename segment
under app_data_dir, so separators, a leading dot and ".." are rejected with
TypeError '[system] store.name must be a file-safe namespace — received "...".'
dispose() (at app.stop()) saves and closes the Tauri Store resource.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.2 tray — plugin name "tray", subpath "@moku-labs/system/tray"
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Desktop system tray. The web provider is all-"unsupported" (no browser tray API) and the
Tauri provider is gated by a desktop ALLOWLIST — only macos/windows/linux get the real
provider, while ios/android/unknown get a typed absence — both absence branches coming
from the same unsupportedProvider() factory. On Tauri desktop the OS icon is created
lazily on the first mutating call; exactly one Menu is kept alive (setMenu closes the one
it replaced); dispose() destroys icon + menu at app.stop().

src/plugins/tray/types.ts:

  /** Tray identity config. */
  export type TrayConfig = {
    /** OS-level tray identity. Validated non-empty at onInit. Default: "moku-system". */
    id: string;
    /**
     * Status-item image: a path the app process can read, or bytes. Omit it to use the
     * app's default window icon (defaultWindowIcon() from @tauri-apps/api/app) — the
     * reliable default, since a relative path resolves against the process working
     * directory, which a bundled app does not control. A macOS status item created with
     * no icon at all is invisible. A missing image file resolves
     * err("tauri", "unavailable", <message naming tray.icon>).
     */
    icon?: string;
  };

  /** Isomorphic tray menu item. action runs in the webview on click (Tauri desktop only). */
  export type TrayMenuItem = {
    /** Stable item identity. */
    id: string;
    /** Visible label. */
    text: string;
    /** Enabled state; defaults to true. */
    enabled?: boolean;
    /** Click handler (Tauri desktop only). */
    action?: () => void;
  };

  /** Internal tray state — the resolution slot. */
  export type TrayState = ResolutionState<TrayProvider>;

  /** Desktop tray API. Web and Tauri-mobile return err("unsupported") from every method. */
  export type TrayApi = {
    /** Replace the tray menu. First mutating call creates the OS icon lazily. */
    setMenu: (items: TrayMenuItem[]) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
    /** Set hover tooltip text. */
    setTooltip: (text: string) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
    /** Set the tray icon by path (path resolution is the native packager's contract). */
    setIcon: (iconPath: string) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
    /** Remove the tray icon; next mutating call recreates it. ok even if never created. */
    destroy: () => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
  };

onInit: throws TypeError "[system] tray.id must be a non-empty string." when
config.id.trim() === "".

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.3 notify — plugin name "notify", subpath "@moku-labs/system/notify"
--------------------------------------------------------------------
OS/browser notifications — the v1 core trio only (Tauri mobile scheduling/channel
methods are out of scope). Permission flow is explicit by contract: show() NEVER
auto-prompts — err("denied") when permission is not granted; the app must call
requestPermission() deliberately. NO config (excluded from pluginConfigs).

src/plugins/notify/types.ts:

  /** Notification content. */
  export type NotifyOptions = {
    /** Notification title. */
    title: string;
    /** Optional body text. */
    body?: string;
  };

  /** Internal notify state — the resolution slot. */
  export type NotifyState = ResolutionState<NotifyProvider>;

  /** Notification API — explicit permission flow; show() never auto-prompts. */
  export type NotifyApi = {
    /** Whether notification permission is currently granted. */
    isPermissionGranted: () => Promise<SystemResult<boolean>>;
    /** Prompt the user for notification permission. */
    requestPermission: () => Promise<SystemResult<boolean>>;
    /** Show a notification. Never auto-prompts — err("denied") when permission is not granted. */
    show: (options: NotifyOptions) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
  };

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.4 clipboard — plugin name "clipboard", subpath "@moku-labs/system/clipboard"
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Text-only clipboard (image/HTML out of scope — not isomorphic even within Tauri). The
web provider feature-probes navigator.clipboard (absent in insecure contexts ->
"unsupported") and maps NotAllowedError -> "denied"; deliberately does NOT rely on
permissions.query. NO config (excluded from pluginConfigs).

src/plugins/clipboard/types.ts:

  /** Internal clipboard state — the resolution slot. */
  export type ClipboardState = ResolutionState<ClipboardProvider>;

  /**
   * Clipboard text API. NotAllowedError maps to err("denied"); support is
   * feature-probed (no permissions.query).
   */
  export type ClipboardApi = {
    /** Read clipboard text. */
    readText: () => Promise<SystemResult<string>>;
    /** Write clipboard text. */
    writeText: (text: string) => Promise<SystemResult<void>>;
  };

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.5 deepLink — plugin name "deepLink", subpath "@moku-labs/system/deep-link"
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Deep-link URL delivery — the only push-driven capability, and the only plugin that
declares events. Dedup is REPLAY-ONLY: the first delivery is dropped when it equals the
launch URL getCurrent() recorded, and the window closes immediately; a later repeat of
the same URL is a real user action and IS delivered. On the web, getCurrent() reads an
explicit ?deeplink= / #deeplink= parameter off the page URL (percent-encoded) and
resolves ok(null) for an ordinary visit — the page's own address is never a deep link.
Naming: plugin name string "deepLink", directory deep-link/, event "deepLink:open".

src/plugins/deep-link/types.ts:

  /** Deep-link scheme allowlist. */
  export type DeepLinkConfig = {
    /** Allowed URI schemes; empty = accept all. Validated at onInit (lowercase scheme pattern). */
    schemes: string[];
  };

  /** Typed per-plugin events (visible to this plugin + future depends-declared plugins). */
  export type DeepLinkEvents = {
    /** A deep-link URL was delivered to the running app (post-dedup, post-filter). */
    "deepLink:open": { url: string };
  };

  /** Unsubscribe function returned by onOpen. */
  export type Unsubscribe = () => void;

  /** Internal deep-link state — resolution slot + launch-replay guard + island subscribers. */
  export type DeepLinkState = ResolutionState<DeepLinkProvider> & {
    /** The launch URL as read by getCurrent() — what the one-time replay is compared against. */
    launchUrl: string | null;
    /** Whether the first delivery has been seen, closing the one-time replay window. */
    launchReplayDone: boolean;
    /** onOpen() callbacks, notified after dedup + scheme filtering. */
    subscribers: Set<(payload: { url: string }) => void>;
  };

  /** Deep-link API — launch URL + runtime delivery subscription. */
  export type DeepLinkApi = {
    /** The URL the app was launched with, scheme-filtered; ok(null) when none. */
    getCurrent: () => Promise<SystemResult<string | null>>;
    /**
     * Subscribe to runtime deliveries. Local + synchronous (always succeeds); on web
     * no push deliveries occur in v1.
     */
    onOpen: (cb: (payload: { url: string }) => void) => Unsubscribe;
  };

onInit: each entry of config.schemes must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$/ — otherwise
TypeError '[system] deepLink.schemes entries must be lowercase URI schemes (e.g. "myapp").'

Cross-repo note: on Windows/Linux the OS delivers deep-link URLs as CLI args to a NEW
process instance; single-instance forwarding is wired by the native packager repo.
Until then, runtime deliveries on Windows/Linux may not arrive.

====================================================================
5. Event catalog
====================================================================

Framework-level Events: Record<string, never> — intentionally empty in v1. Capability
events are per-plugin and depends-gated, never promoted to the framework contract.

  event           | payload            | emitted by | when
  --------------- | ------------------ | ---------- | -----------------------------------
  "deepLink:open" | { url: string }    | deepLink   | a deep-link URL is delivered to the
                  |                    |            | running app (post-dedup, post-scheme-
                  |                    |            | filter)

Islands/apps consume deliveries via app.deepLink.onOpen(cb). Plugins that declare
depends: [deepLinkPlugin] additionally see the typed "deepLink:open" event in hooks
(v1 ships no such edge — the event is island/app-facing plumbing).

The other four capabilities are pure request/response and declare no events.

====================================================================
6. Config schema & defaults (pluginConfigs)
====================================================================

Framework Config is Record<string, never> (empty in v1) — capabilities configure via
pluginConfigs, keyed by plugin name string:

  pluginConfigs: {
    runtime?:  { forceKind: "tauri" | "web" | null;        // default null (auto-detect)
                 forcePlatform: RuntimePlatform | null },   // default null (auto-detect)
    store?:    { name: string },                            // default "moku-system";
                                                            // /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/i
    tray?:     { id: string; icon?: string },               // id default "moku-system",
                                                            // non-empty; no icon = the app's
                                                            // default window icon
    deepLink?: { schemes: string[] }                        // default [] (= accept all);
                                                            // lowercase scheme pattern
  }

notify and clipboard take NO config — they have no pluginConfigs entry.

====================================================================
7. Lifecycle & provider resolution semantics
====================================================================

  const app = createApp({ plugins: [...], pluginConfigs: {...} });
    - onInit validation runs; bad config throws TypeError synchronously (fail-fast).
  await app.start();
    - each capability's onStart kicks off FIRE-AND-FORGET provider resolution
      (startResolution): an unawaited promise is stored in the plugin's state slot.
    - selection happens inside the loader: ctx.runtime.kind === "tauri" -> dynamic
      import of the @tauri-apps/* plugin; "web" -> web implementation;
      unsupported combinations -> unsupportedProvider() stand-in.
    - load() rejections are folded into the promise as reason "unavailable" — start()
      never throws for environmental reasons.
  await app.<capability>.<method>(...)
    - awaits the resolution slot (awaitProvider), then delegates to the provider.
    - before start(): resolves to { ok: false, reason: "unavailable",
      message: "app not started — call app.start() first" }.
  await app.stop();
    - stopResolution flips a stopped sentinel and awaits the resolved provider's
      dispose() (tray destroys the OS icon; deepLink unregisters the OS listener).
    - a provider that finishes resolving AFTER stop is disposed immediately and the
      slot resolves to "unavailable" ("stopped during resolution").
    - teardown registries are per-app-instance (keyed by the app's frozen global
      config object) — multiple app instances never share resolution state.

====================================================================
8. Error-handling patterns
====================================================================

Discriminant narrowing — the canonical consumer pattern:

  const r = await system.store.get<number>("count");
  if (r.ok) {
    // r: SystemOk<number | undefined> — r.value, r.provider
    use(r.value ?? 0);
  } else {
    // r: SystemErr — r.reason, r.provider, r.message?
    switch (r.reason) {
      case "unsupported": hideFeature(); break;          // permanent — don't retry
      case "denied":      explainPermission(); break;    // user/platform said no
      case "unavailable": scheduleRetry(); break;        // transient/environmental
      case "error":       report(r.message); break;      // provider threw; raw message
    }
  }

Permission flow (notify) — show() never auto-prompts:

  const granted = await system.notify.isPermissionGranted();
  if (granted.ok && !granted.value) {
    const asked = await system.notify.requestPermission();  // deliberate user gesture
    if (!asked.ok || !asked.value) return;                  // denied — stop here
  }
  const shown = await system.notify.show({ title: "Done" });
  if (!shown.ok && shown.reason === "denied") {
    // permission revoked between check and show — still just data
  }

Feature-gating by capability, not by runtime — never branch on ctx.runtime in islands;
probe the result instead:

  const probe = await system.tray.setTooltip("ready");
  const hasTray = probe.ok || probe.reason !== "unsupported";

Programmer errors still throw:

  createApp({ plugins: [storePlugin], pluginConfigs: { store: { name: "../escape" } } });
  // -> TypeError: [system] store.name must be a file-safe namespace — received "../escape".

====================================================================
9. Usage examples
====================================================================

Multi-capability app (web + native, one codebase):

  import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/system";
  import { clipboardPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/clipboard";
  import { deepLinkPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/deep-link";
  import { notifyPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/notify";
  import { storePlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/store";
  import { trayPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/tray";

  const system = createApp({
    plugins: [storePlugin, trayPlugin, notifyPlugin, clipboardPlugin, deepLinkPlugin],
    pluginConfigs: {
      store: { name: "my-app" },
      tray: { id: "my-app-tray" },
      deepLink: { schemes: ["myapp"] }
      // notify + clipboard: no config
    }
  });

  await system.start();

  // persistence — identical call sites on both providers (JsonValue-constrained)
  await system.store.set("session", { user: "alex", visits: 3 });
  const session = await system.store.get<{ user: string; visits: number }>("session");

  // tray — ok on Tauri desktop, typed "unsupported" on web / Tauri mobile
  await system.tray.setMenu([
    { id: "open", text: "Open", action: () => focusWindow() },
    { id: "quit", text: "Quit", action: () => system.tray.destroy() }
  ]);

  // clipboard
  const copied = await system.clipboard.writeText("hello");
  if (!copied.ok && copied.reason === "denied") toast("Clipboard blocked");

  // deep links — launch URL once, then live deliveries
  const launch = await system.deepLink.getCurrent();
  if (launch.ok && launch.value !== null) route(launch.value);
  const unsubscribe = system.deepLink.onOpen(({ url }) => route(url));

  // teardown (disposes providers, removes the tray icon, unhooks OS listeners)
  unsubscribe();
  await system.stop();

Deterministic tests — force the seam:

  import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/system";
  import { storePlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/store";

  // Hoisted: `runtime` is a core plugin, so it is not a typed pluginConfigs key of
  // createApp. A hoisted (non-fresh) object passes the check, and the kernel applies it.
  const pluginConfigs = {
    store: { name: "test-db" },
    runtime: { forceKind: "web", forcePlatform: "macos" }
  } as const;

  const app = createApp({ plugins: [storePlugin], pluginConfigs });
  await app.start();
  const r = await app.store.set("k", 1);
  // r === { ok: true, value: undefined, provider: "web" }

Constructing results (ok / err helpers, e.g. in test doubles):

  import { err, ok, type SystemResult } from "@moku-labs/system";
  const success: SystemResult<number> = ok(42, "web");
  const failure: SystemResult<number> = err("tauri", "unavailable", "plugin not registered");

====================================================================
10. Extension pattern (createPlugin)
====================================================================

createPlugin defines a consumer (Layer 3) plugin bound to this framework's types. Its
ctx carries the three core-plugin injections — ctx.log (structured logging, MC2),
ctx.env (validated environment access, MC3), and ctx.runtime (the seam):

  import { createApp, createPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system";

  const telemetryPlugin = createPlugin("telemetry", {
    config: { endpoint: "https://example.test/ingest" },
    api: ctx => ({
      report: (event: string) => {
        // never console.* / process.env — family conventions MC2/MC3
        ctx.log.info("telemetry event", { event, shell: ctx.runtime.kind });
      }
    })
  });

  const app = createApp({ plugins: [telemetryPlugin] });
  app.telemetry.report("boot");

Rules for extensions:
  - Types infer from the spec object — no explicit generics.
  - Use ctx.runtime for shell/platform decisions inside plugins; keep islands
    runtime-agnostic (probe SystemResult instead).
  - If your plugin wraps a native API, follow the capability anatomy: structural local
    provider types, SystemResult on every method, fire-and-forget resolution in
    onStart, dispose() in onStop.

====================================================================
11. Peer dependencies, web bundling & environment
====================================================================

Dependencies (bundled): @moku-labs/core 1.5.0, @moku-labs/common 0.3.0, idb-keyval 6.3.0.

Optional peer dependencies — ONLY needed in the native (Tauri) shell; dynamically
imported inside Tauri providers; pure-web consumers skip them entirely:

  @tauri-apps/api                        ^2.11.0
  @tauri-apps/plugin-store               ^2.4.0    (store)
  @tauri-apps/plugin-notification        ^2.3.0    (notify)
  @tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager   ^2.3.0    (clipboard)
  @tauri-apps/plugin-deep-link           ^2.4.0    (deepLink)

Bundling for the web: every providers/index.ts reaches its Tauri provider through a lazy
import("./tauri") — there is no static import of a @tauri-apps/* package anywhere outside
providers/tauri.ts, so the native code sits in chunks a web build never executes. The
bundler still has to RESOLVE the specifiers, so a web-only build either installs the
optional peers or marks them external:

  Bun:          Bun.build({ entrypoints: [...], external: ["@tauri-apps/*"] })
  Vite/Rollup:  build: { rollupOptions: { external: /^@tauri-apps\// } }

Environment: Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.3.14 (bun exclusively — never npm/yarn/pnpm).
TypeScript strict mode with exactOptionalPropertyTypes and noUncheckedIndexedAccess.
Tests: vitest, unit + integration projects, 90% coverage threshold; plugin tests are
colocated in src/plugins/<name>/__tests__/{unit,integration}/; root tests/ is for
framework-level integration only.

====================================================================
12. Native permissions (Tauri ACL) & cross-repo naming
====================================================================

A capability that reaches the OS needs a Tauri ACL permission in the app's capability
file plus a Rust-side plugin. @moku-labs/native codegens exactly these — capability file,
Cargo dependencies, plugin registrations — from the system plugins the app composes.

  capability | ACL permissions                             | Rust
  ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | -----------------------------
  store      | store:default                               | tauri-plugin-store,
             |                                             | tauri_plugin_store::Builder
             |                                             | ::default().build()
  notify     | notification:default                        | tauri-plugin-notification, init()
  clipboard  | clipboard-manager:allow-read-text,          | tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager,
             | clipboard-manager:allow-write-text          | init()
  deepLink   | deep-link:default, core:event:default       | tauri-plugin-deep-link, init(),
             |                                             | schemes in the Tauri config
  tray       | core:tray:default, core:menu:default,       | no crate — Cargo features
             | core:image:default, core:resources:default  | tray-icon + image-png,
             |                                             | desktop targets only

  - clipboard-manager:default grants NOTHING; the two allow-* permissions are the real
    ones.
  - The core:* entries (tray's four, and core:event:default) all ship inside core:default.
  - Deep links on Windows/Linux additionally need single-instance forwarding, wired by
    the packager.

Cross-repo naming — @moku-labs/native keys its config.system by the Tauri plugin name,
which is not always this framework's plugin name:

  system plugin | native config.system
  ------------- | --------------------
  store         | store
  notify        | notification
  clipboard     | clipboard-manager
  tray          | tray
  deepLink      | deep-link
